name: Wankhede Stadium
pitchType: Red soil with true bounce, carry & pace; evening sea breeze assists swing
historicMoment: Hosted 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup Final; MS Dhoni struck the match-winning six.

name: Lord's Cricket Ground
pitchType: Famous 8-foot (2.5m) natural slope running south-to-north; true bounce & swing
historicMoment: Known as the 'Home of Cricket'; hosted 2019 World Cup Final with the Super Over finish.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)
pitchType: Drop-in pitch offering even bounce and pace; colossal boundary dimensions
historicMoment: Hosted the first-ever Test match in 1877; 1992 and 2015 ICC World Cup Finals.

name: Eden Gardens
pitchType: Good batting track with reliable bounce; aids orthodox spinners as match progresses
historicMoment: VVS Laxman's 281 in 2001 vs Australia; Rohit Sharma's world record 264 in 2014.

name: The Oval (Kia Oval)
pitchType: Traditionally one of the fastest, bounciest pitches in England with exceptional carry
historicMoment: Birthplace of The Ashes in 1882; traditionally hosts the final Test of the English summer.

name: Sydney Cricket Ground (SCG)
pitchType: Historic bulli soil providing classic turn for spinners from Day 3 onwards
historicMoment: Traditional New Year's Pink Test; famous heritage Members Pavilion and clock tower.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
pitchType: Features both red-soil and black-soil wickets; expansive 63-acre complex
historicMoment: Largest cricket stadium in the world; hosted the 2023 ICC World Cup Final.

name: HPCA Stadium
pitchType: High altitude (1,457m) Ryegrass outfield; brisk chill aids extra pace and lateral swing
historicMoment: Set against the dramatic snow-capped Dhauladhar mountain range in Himachal Pradesh.

name: Newlands Cricket Ground
pitchType: Seamer-friendly conditions on opening days; takes spin later under Mediterranean sun
historicMoment: Overlooked by the majestic Table Mountain and Devil's Peak; iconic Test venue.

name: Kensington Oval
pitchType: Hard, true bounce and fast outfield; Mecca of West Indian cricket heritage
historicMoment: Hosted the 2007 ICC World Cup Final and the 2024 ICC T20 World Cup Final.

name: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium
pitchType: Flat batting paradise with short boundaries (60m square) and high-altitude thin air
historicMoment: Chris Gayle's record 175* off 66 balls in IPL 2013; first stadium in world to use solar power.

name: M. A. Chidambaram Stadium (Chepauk)
pitchType: Dry clay surface offering intense spin and low bounce; humid coastal air
historicMoment: Historic Tied Test between India and Australia in 1986; yellow fortress of CSK.

name: Trent Bridge
pitchType: Pungent heavy atmosphere encourages heavy swing; ultra-fast outfield and high scoring
historicMoment: Venue of England's world record 481/6 vs Australia; Stuart Broad 8/15 in 2015 Ashes.

name: Adelaide Oval
pitchType: Famous drop-in pitch with very short square boundaries and lengthy straight boundaries
historicMoment: Hosted the first-ever Day/Night pink-ball Test match in cricket history (2015).

name: Gaddafi Stadium
pitchType: Classic subcontinent surface; flat early with reverse swing emerging later
historicMoment: Hosted the 1996 Cricket World Cup Final where Sri Lanka lifted their maiden title.

name: Galle International Stadium
pitchType: Coastal breezes off Indian Ocean aid seam early, turning into an explosive spin minefield
historicMoment: Bordered on two sides by the Indian Ocean and the 17th-century UNESCO Dutch Fort.

name: Dubai International Stadium
pitchType: Fair contest between bat and ball; renowned for evening dew factor
historicMoment: Distinguished by its circular 'Ring of Fire' roof lighting system of 350 floodlights.

name: Old Trafford
pitchType: Quickest and bounciest pitch in England; retains reverse swing and spin late in Tests
historicMoment: Shane Warne bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting here in the 1993 Ashes.

name: SuperSport Park
pitchType: High-altitude fast track with sharp steepling bounce and rapid outfield
historicMoment: Fortress for South African fast bowling with picturesque open grass banks.

name: Edgbaston Cricket Ground
pitchType: Lively pace and reliable bounce; famous for vibrant, vocal Eric Hollies Stand atmosphere
historicMoment: Site of the dramatic 2005 Ashes Test thriller where England won by just 2 runs.
